blocks.text: Bulkheads isolate resources so that one overloaded or failing part of a system does not consume all available capacity.
Services, dependencies, or tenants can have separate thread pools, connection pools, or concurrency limits. A concurrency limit caps work running at the same time.
An application gives its reporting service and payment service separate connection pools.
Slow reports can exhaust the reporting pool while payments still have connections available.
When an isolated pool is full, new work may be rejected or wait in a bounded queue.
Separate pools can leave capacity unused in one area while another area is busy.
Bulkheads limit the spread of failures. Circuit breakers stop calls to a failing dependency; rate limiting controls how much work is admitted over time.
